text: Not every number you can compute deserves a spot on a dashboard. Here's how to tell the difference.
One test, applied metric by metric. If the honest answer is no, it's interesting, not actionable — it belongs in a report someone can drill into, not the handful of numbers checked every day.
A dashboard crowded with everything available doesn't communicate more — it communicates that nothing was worth prioritizing. Fewer, well-chosen KPIs beat a longer list that just gets skimmed past.
And a genuine KPI needs a target to compare against, not just a raw value — that's exactly why the KPI visual exists as something distinct from a plain card.
Next: dashboard layout and visual hierarchy — where the KPIs you just chose actually go on the page.
